papers.title: Frozen Models, Evolving Expertise: Model-Agnostic Learning from Deployment Experience for Multimodal Medical AI

summary.tldr: A model-agnostic framework enables frozen LLMs and VLMs to learn from online deployment experience without fine-tuning, using dynamic skill, textual knowledge, and multimodal memories.
key_points: Utilizes three external expertise components: a Skill guide for reasoning/tool use, a Knowledge Memory for facts, and a Multimodal Knowledge Base linking visual examples to current input images.
Employs an online validation strategy that retains experience updates only if they improve performance on new cases without causing regression on prior ones, avoiding fixed validation sets.
Achieves up to a 34.2% online performance improvement on medical tasks across four open-weight and closed-source base models.

Demonstrates generalizability to unseen cases, zero-shot transferability of learned experience to other models without re-optimization, and domain adaptability to non-medical visual reasoning across six total benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deployed, black-box multimodal AI models to continuously adapt to evolving clinical knowledge and visual data without computationally expensive model re-training or weight access.

papers.title: EDiS: Edge Disjoint Subgraph Sparsification Framework for Graph Neural Networks

summary.tldr: EDiS decouples GNN graph sparsification into a one-time decomposition into edge-disjoint subgraphs and a fast per-epoch recombination step to dynamic sparse topologies without repeated structural extraction.
key_points: Decomposes the graph once into cacheable edge-disjoint subgraphs using feature-based scores and successive maximum score covering forests.
Recombines cached subgraphs per epoch to satisfy target edge-budget constraints and retention ratios without re-extracting structure.
Provides combinatorial analysis proving the deterministic preservation of high-score cut edges under the default covering-forest selector.
Outperformed 17 baselines across 19 homophilic, heterophilic, and large-scale node classification benchmarks under identical edge budgets, showing maximum gain at tight edge constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the computational overhead of dynamic graph sampling in sparse GNN training while avoiding the performance degradation associated with fixed sparse topologies.

papers.title: CARE: Certifying Acceleration for Vision-Language-Action Inference

summary.tldr: CARE is a certified accelerator selection framework that provides finite-sample risk guarantees on acceleration-induced failures by evaluating paired closed-loop rollouts between accelerated and reference vision-language-action policies.
key_points: Defines acceleration-induced failure by comparing paired rollouts from identical initial conditions, tracking cases where the reference policy succeeds but the accelerated policy fails.
Provides finite-sample guarantees using a calibration set to deploy the fastest candidate that keeps failure risk within a user-specified budget, falling back to the reference model if none qualify.
Uses sequential testing and failure-triggered reference rollouts to reduce certification compute costs by 78.9% compared to exhaustive evaluation.
Demonstrates 9.0–10.8x speedups on LIBERO suites using OpenVLA-OFT, preserving at least 85.8% of reference-solved episodes at 95% confidence.
Generalizes across diverse mechanisms including flow-step reduction for π_{0.5} and LLM agent acceleration for Qwen3.5-9B and Llama-3.1-8B in Crafter.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables safe, aggressive compute reduction in real-time robot control without risking unquantified task failures caused by information loss in accelerated models.

papers.title: You Changed Your Mind, The Model Didn't: Demystifying Intent in Multi-Turn Dialogue

summary.tldr: Intent-Eval is a benchmark revealing that LLMs fail in multi-turn dialogues by treating rejected or superseded user proposals as active requirements, a failure mitigated by the proposed Intent-OPSD self-distillation framework.
key_points: Models suffer from mentioned-as-in-effect confusion, where mentioning a rejected change causes task derailment even when final user intent is unchanged.
Intent-Eval benchmarks evolving user intent across four domains: tool actions, code, databases, and mathematics.
Accuracy degradation caused by obsolete requirements persists or deepens over extended multi-turn interactions.
Intent-OPSD uses a frozen Teacher model initialized from the same base to provide active-intent supervision to a Student trained on full dialogue histories.
summary.why_it_matters: Language models need mechanisms to explicitly filter out discarded proposals to accurately execute multi-turn tasks where user requirements evolve.

papers.title: The Lattice of Transition Laws

summary.tldr: Researchers frame diffusion and autoregressive decoding as paths on a corruption lattice, using data geometry and pretrained weight kernels to predict optimal decoding schedules without running decoding.
key_points: Models diffusion, autoregression, and hybrid approaches as paths on a unified corruption lattice where schedule cost is the discarded dependence between parallel steps.
Proves that zero-cost schedules require a minimum number of steps equal to the data's treedepth (logarithmic for sequences, linear for grid side lengths) based on underlying Markov graph geometry.
Formulates a method using a pairwise dependence kernel estimated directly from pretrained weights to rank positive-cost decoding schedules before execution.
Validates schedule ranking predictions empirically across text, image, and video generation benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a theoretical design principle to optimize and predict the step-efficiency of decoding schedules across diffusion, autoregressive, and hybrid generative architectures prior to inference.

papers.title: Skill Constellations: Tracing the Supply Chain of Agent Skills on GitHub

summary.tldr: Researchers built the first dated copy network of AI agent skills, analyzing 2,193,119 SKILL.md adoptions across GitHub to trace unversioned skill provenance and propagation.
key_points: Skill propagation on GitHub operates without central registries, versions, or provenance, causing security fixes at the source to rarely reach copied skills.
A small subset of repositories acts as the origin for nearly all copied skills, and GitHub star counts fail to identify these primary sources.

The authors developed a predictive model to rank high-source repositories for security auditing, where auditing the top 100 model-ranked repositories prevented 14.9% of subsequent high-risk skill adoptions compared to 0.5% when auditing the top 100 most-starred repositories.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings show that platforms must move to versioned references rather than raw copies to prevent the unmonitored spread of vulnerable or malicious code across AI agent workflows.

papers.title: Predicting Cable Dynamics with Physical Attention Bias

summary.tldr: A physical attention bias using arc-length and Euclidean distances improves learned cable simulators' generalizability to unseen cables and reduces long-rollout error.
key_points: DLO contact and elastic forces depend on two separate pairwise metrics: Euclidean distance in 3D space and arc-length distance along the cable.
The physical attention bias adds an additive term with a learned rate directly to the attention logits without altering the rest of the model architecture.
Using arc-length bias alone reduces prediction error by 15% and cuts segment length drift by more than half when attention is the sole mechanism connecting distant segments.
Assigning arc-length and Euclidean distance biases to disjoint sets of attention heads yielded the best or near-best performance across all evaluation metrics.
summary.why_it_matters: Incorporating structural geometric biases into attention mechanisms significantly improves the stability and generalization of neural physics simulators for deformable objects.

papers.title: MARGIN: Runtime Confidence Calibration for Multi-Agent Foundation Model Coordination

summary.tldr: MARGIN introduces a runtime calibration method that incrementally adjusts multi-agent model confidence scores based on observed outcomes, improving collective decision accuracy without model retraining.
key_points: MARGIN calculates confidence corrections using the ratio of recent accuracy to stated confidence within specific confidence bands, blending sparse bands with a model-level estimate.
On BigCodeBench, uncalibrated model-mean confidence negatively correlated with accuracy, resulting in below-chance performance when selecting the more confident responder.

Evaluated across code generation, QA, and math tasks using up to 18 models, MARGIN achieved lower post-shift expected calibration error (ECE) than online baselines in multiple distribution-shift transitions.

Applying MARGIN's calibrated confidence weighting improved multi-agent answer-selection accuracy by 4.3 and 14.0 percentage points on two code-generation benchmarks compared to uncalibrated weighting.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables heterogeneous multi-agent systems to dynamically correct miscalibrated self-reported model confidence at runtime using correctness feedback, directly improving ensemble decision accuracy under shifting workloads.

papers.title: SPW-Nav: A Streaming Panoramic World Model for Language-Guided Navigation

summary.tldr: SPW-Nav is a streaming panoramic world model that generates one minute of 2K 360-degree video in real time from a single panorama based on language-guided movement instructions.
key_points: Uses spherical rotation decoupling to apply exact rotation directly on the sphere.
Employs pose-aligned conditioning to keep translation inputs bounded during long video streams.
Combines multi-term memory with a few-step generator to maintain scene continuity through on-the-fly instruction changes.
Introduces SPW-NavSet, a dataset of panoramic videos paired with camera trajectories and verified text instructions.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables interactive, long-duration 360-degree scene exploration driven by dynamic text instructions for VR applications and embodied agent training.

papers.title: Evaluating the Transfer of Co-Evolved Communication from 2D to 3D Simulation

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated the transfer of a co-evolved multi-robot communication mechanism from a discrete 2D simulator to a physics-based 3D environment, analyzing time budgets, social cues, and role asymmetry.
key_points: Success rate scaled approximately linearly with episode time budget between 2,000 and 6,000 physics steps without plateauing, indicating shorter runs underestimate controller performance.
The co-evolved social cue served primarily as a jam-assistance mechanism rather than a navigation guide across both 2D and 3D environments, though the effect was stronger in 2D.
Across eight independent evolutionary runs, a consistent direction of agent asymmetry was observed; controlling the agent processing order confirmed this was not a physics engine artifact.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that co-evolved communication roles retain their functionality when transferring from 2D to 3D environments helps bridge the gap between simplified evolutionary simulations and realistic physical robotics.

papers.title: Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization

summary.tldr: ZIP-SR and ZE-EDEN redesign 4-bit AdamW optimizer state quantization by rounding second-moment states in preconditioner space rather than state space.
key_points: Identifies that minimizing state-space quantization error in AdamW's second moment does not guarantee minimal preconditioner error for subsequent adaptive updates.

Introduces Zero-Inclusive Preconditioner-space Stochastic Rounding (ZIP-SR), which retains zero in the second-moment codebook and computes stochastic rounding probabilities directly in preconditioner space.
Introduces Zero-Excluding EDEN calibration (ZE-EDEN), which utilizes a zero-excluding codebook and rescales quantized second-moment blocks to counter distortion from positive quantization floors.
Applies 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) to first moments with targeted stochastic rounding on the LM-head during the final 10% of training.
Reduces the validation-loss gap to 32-bit AdamW by up to 70% compared to TorchAO 4-bit AdamW across 130M to 2.7B parameter pretraining and supervised fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves the performance and training stability of memory-efficient 4-bit AdamW optimization without requiring additional memory overhead.

papers.title: DiffuPlex: Accelerating Full-Duplex Spoken Dialog Models via Rolling Masked Diffusion

summary.tldr: DiffuPlex accelerates full-duplex spoken dialog models using a rolling masked diffusion framework to predict multiple future interaction frames in a single backbone step.
key_points: DiffuPlex predicts multiple future user and assistant frames per step, consuming a confident prefix while maintaining frame-rate interaction.
The system detects interaction divergence as user speech arrives, preserving already played assistant content while revising unplayed future frames.
Evaluated two inference policies: DiffuPlex-LISTEN (consumes future frames during predicted assistant silence) and DiffuPlex-SPEAK (also consumes predicted assistant speech).
Achieved deployment-path wall-clock speedups of 1.46x (LISTEN) and 1.59x (SPEAK), and Core LM speedups of 1.61x (LISTEN) and 1.80x (SPEAK).
All measured backbone invocations complete within the 80ms interaction frame interval.
summary.why_it_matters: DiffuPlex reduces the computational bottleneck of real-time conversational speech models by sub-sampling backbone steps without sacrificing full-duplex responsiveness.

papers.title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement

summary.tldr: The MiMo-V2.6 series introduces an omni-modal foundation model architecture that scales reinforcement learning compute across training batch size, environment diversity, and agentic grading.
key_points: RL compute scaling leverages asynchronous training consuming 1,568 samples and 2.7–3.7 billion tokens per step at context lengths up to 1M.
Training environment spans code, visual, general, and cyber domains using a mixture of agent harnesses for mixed-task agentic RL.
Reward signals use groupwise agentic grading to handle long-horizon tasks and incentivize shorter, token-efficient solutions.
Training stability is maintained by freezing the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) router and enforcing a multi-layer defense against reward hacking.
Infrastructure features a hybrid-Sliding Window Attention (SWA) base, unified trajectory representation, decoupled control and data planes, and high-concurrency rollout.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates concrete infrastructure and algorithmic strategies for scaling reinforcement learning compute stably to advance self-improvement in large omni-modal models.

papers.title: Not Every Change Is Necessary: Recoverable Drift in Large Language Model Unlearning

summary.tldr: Propose-Then-Project Unlearning (PTP-U) addresses collateral model degradation by reversing non-target parameter drift while preserving achieved unlearning performance.
key_points: PTP-U uses a two-stage framework: first applying local analytic edits to weaken target knowledge, then aligning non-target output distributions back to the original model under fixed forgetting constraints.
The framework targets the recovery of non-target capabilities that are accidentally altered during the unlearning process.
Across three benchmarks, PTP-U achieved 81.22%-91.03% forgetting while maintaining an average of 94.20% non-target utility.
PTP-U consistently retained higher non-target utility compared to baseline methods when evaluated at matched forgetting levels.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that collateral utility loss from machine unlearning can be recovered without compromising the intended removal of target knowledge.

papers.title: Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks

summary.tldr: Memento 3 introduces a model-based recursive self-improvement framework where frozen LLM agents continually learn world models by updating natural-language rulebooks and compiling them into verified executable code.
key_points: Maintains an external natural-language rulebook as persistent semantic memory, which is compiled into executable code for environment prediction and planning.
Updates to the compiled code require dual verification: LLM judgment of faithfulness to the rulebook and cell-exact replay of observed transitions.
Employs a population extension that maintains multiple world models in parallel to share interaction evidence and guide exploration.
Achieved 100.0 mean Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE) across all 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games using 44% of human action counts.
Trained a learned feedback controller on Atari Pong that won 21:0 across three evaluated episodes without requiring runtime LLM calls.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that frozen LLMs can achieve continuous, autonomous self-improvement in dynamic environments by grounding symbolic world models into verified executable code without updating neural network weights.

papers.title: Internalizer: Portable Context-to-Parameter Mapping for Very Large Language Models

summary.tldr: The Internalizer is a portable context-to-parameter hypernetwork that generates document-specific LoRA adapters for frozen models up to 284B parameters using a lightweight, transferrable architecture.
key_points: Generates document-specific LoRA adapters for the 284B-parameter DeepSeek v4 Flash via a single forward pass, scaling context-to-parameter mapping by two orders of magnitude.
Uses a model-agnostic trunk with thin model-specific entry and exit layers, enabling cheap initial training on small models before porting to large target models.
Achieves 84.9% top-1 and 97.8% top-5 teacher-forced accuracy on unseen documents up to 4,000 tokens using only a three-word instruction in the context window.
Outperforms the baseline base model accuracy of 63.4% top-1 and 83.5% top-5, and can be served independently or combined with in-window context.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables massive language models to internalize long contexts into weight adapters via a single forward pass, improving retrieval accuracy while drastically reducing context window overhead.

papers.title: Distilling Routed 3D Privilege for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

summary.tldr: Geometry-Privileged Distillation (GPD) improves RGB-only VLM spatial reasoning by distilling text-rendered 3D geometric evidence into the model via on-policy self-distillation on incorrect trajectories.
key_points: Renders depth, semantic, and bird's-eye-view (BEV) cues into compact text and routes them to the teacher alongside the reference answer using question-conditioned routing.
Combines privileged KL divergence—applied exclusively to incorrect trajectories—with GRPO, ensuring the deployed inference model remains strictly RGB-only.
Achieves a score of 57.1 on VSI-Bench and a 37.6 average across MindCube, SPARBench, MMSI-Bench, and ViewSpatial using a 4B parameter backbone.
Outperforms standard GRPO and answer-privileged OPSD, with ablations confirming that restricting distillation to incorrect trajectories outperforms full-context injection.
summary.why_it_matters: GPD enhances spatial reasoning accuracy in VLMs during training without imposing architectural modifications or latency penalties at inference time.

papers.title: Overcoming Prior Barriers: Supervised Fine-Tuning under Long-Tail Distribution

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced the 'prior barrier' concept to quantify long-tail pretraining support disparities in LLMs and proposed PASS, an adaptive instruction selection method that prioritizes budget allocation to weakly supported tail concepts.
key_points: Defined 'prior barrier' to measure how strongly a pretrained model supports competing concepts compared to the target concept during SFT.
Derived a theoretical predictive risk bound showing SFT performance is jointly governed by the prior barrier magnitude and accumulated SFT evidence.

Developed PASS, an SFT instruction selection method that constructs reference-derived concepts, estimates distinguishing instruction evidence, and adaptively allocates budget based on prior barrier demand.
Outperformed seven state-of-the-art instruction selection baselines across four backbone-budget settings, with ablations confirming the superiority of adaptive over uniform allocation.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a theoretical framework and algorithm to optimize SFT dataset selection, ensuring LLMs effectively learn underrepresented tail concepts without wasting compute budget on well-supported head concepts.

papers.title: One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails

summary.tldr: Researchers identified option-channel attacks on typed decision model guardrails, showing that prompt injections or misleading option labels severely increase fail-open error rates while maintaining high model confidence.
key_points: Evaluated seven open-weight typed decision models acting as agent guardrails, finding overall allow-or-block accuracy ranges from 36% to 72% on safety screening tasks.

Injecting six lines of benign server log text raised fail-open error rates from 0% to 63%, while using misleading option names raised fail-open rates to 93%-100% on models placing labels in their input.
Tested defenses failed against targeted attacks, and escalating low-confidence decisions proved ineffective because attack-reversed decisions exhibited equal confidence to correct ones.
Parsing policy fields into typed values allowed a deterministic rule to achieve 100% accuracy across all six policies, rendering the decision model redundant.
summary.why_it_matters: Typed decision models are fundamentally vulnerable to adversarial text and option manipulation, meaning they cannot serve as reliable final arbiters for agent guardrails.

papers.title: DVD: Dynamic Vector Decoding for Efficient MLLM-based Perception

summary.tldr: Dynamic Vector Decoding (DVD) unifies 2D and 3D MLLM perception by converting 2D boxes, 2D masks, and 3D boxes into 1D vector sequences mapped to high-dimensional discrete tokens.
key_points: Transforms diverse perception outputs (2D bounding boxes, 2D masks, 3D bounding boxes) into 1D vector sequences.
Maps 1D vector sequences to compact discrete tokens in a high-dimensional space to bypass text-coordinate overhead and fixed-range quantization constraints.
Uses a lightweight de-tokenizer to decode MLLM output tokens back into target 2D and 3D spatial representations.
Validated on 2D and 3D benchmarks including RefCOCO, SUN-RGBD, KITTI, Hypersim, and nuScenes, reducing token overhead and inference latency.
summary.why_it_matters: DVD enables efficient, high-precision 2D and 3D spatial localization in MLLMs by significantly reducing visual token overhead and latency compared to text-coordinate baseline approaches.

papers.title: AdaCast: Conditional Parameter Generation for Adaptive Time Series Forecasting

summary.tldr: AdaCast introduces a dynamic adaptation framework that uses a generator to produce input-specific, low-rank parameter updates for frozen time-series foundation models during training and inference.
key_points: Static adaptation methods apply a single dataset-level parameter update, failing to adjust to heterogeneous input dynamics.
AdaCast generates conditional low-rank parameter updates tailored to the temporal patterns and seasonality of individual input time series.
The base pretrained time-series foundation model (TSFM) remains frozen while the generator produces dynamic parameters.
Tested across six public benchmarks, AdaCast outperforms static adaptation in in-domain forecasting and improves zero-shot generalization on held-out datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: By generating dynamic, input-specific model weights on the fly, AdaCast allows time-series foundation models to better forecast highly diverse and shifting temporal data.

papers.title: When Has a Bayesian Neural Network Sampled Enough? Adaptive Inference Time with Statistical Guarantees

summary.tldr: A new method uses confidence sequences to dynamically stop Monte Carlo sampling in Bayesian neural networks, providing statistical guarantees while reducing overall latency.
key_points: Replaces fixed Monte Carlo sampling budgets per input with dynamic sampling governed by confidence sequences.
Provides statistical guarantees for downstream tasks including top-class identification, full predictive distribution approximation, and probability-threshold decisions.
Dynamically allocates compute by drawing more samples for ambiguous inputs and fewer for unambiguous inputs.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves inference efficiency in Bayesian neural networks by reducing overall computational budget and latency without sacrificing decision reliability.

papers.title: Use and Disuse: Intent-Structured Experience Consolidation for Memory and Learning in LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Hippocam is a hierarchical memory and continual learning architecture that organizes LLM agent experiences into nested intents and applies recursive prefix consolidation without updating model parameters.
key_points: Structures continuous agent operations into nested intents, consolidating completed intents into task-relevant outcomes and states while keeping active context focused on current goals.
Employs a recursive prefix consolidation mechanism that progressively abstracts long-unused history while preserving original interactions for detailed retrieval.
Allows agents to retrieve details dynamically through the hierarchy and stop once sufficient information is found.
Reinforces, supplements, and updates recalled experiences by reconsolidating them alongside new experiences through a dynamic of use and disuse.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-term autonomous LLM agents to continuously learn, consolidate memory, and evolve skills directly from their own experiences without requiring model parameter updates.

papers.title: Universal Textual Teaching for LLMs

summary.tldr: Universal Textual Teaching (UTT) distills Teacher-Student knowledge gaps into an interpretable natural-language artifact called a Primer without updating Student parameters.
key_points: UTT uses a multi-role pipeline consisting of a Student, Prompter, Teacher, and Synthesizer to iteratively build and consolidate validated lessons into the Primer prompt.
On KernelBench, UTT improves Student accuracy from 9.4% to 48.6% and Fast1 accuracy from 9% to 35%.
On Omni-MATH-2, UTT increases mathematical reasoning accuracy from 27.6% to 51.7%.
Synthesized Primers demonstrate cross-model generalizability, transferring effectively to non-participating Student models.
summary.why_it_matters: UTT enables cross-architecture, reusable knowledge distillation for closed-source or cost-prohibitive API-only language models by operating entirely via prompt manipulation.

papers.title: One Block, Multiple Depths: Recurrent Vision Transformers with Depth-Programmed Experts

summary.tldr: reViT introduces recurrent Vision Transformers using depth-programmed expert mixtures within a single Transformer block, achieving full-depth ViT accuracy without intermediate feature distillation.
key_points: FFN blocks at each recurrent step are parameterized as convex combinations of a shared expert bank, controlled by a continuous normalized-depth coordinate.
Weight-space merging outperformed token-dispatch and output-mixture MoE approaches for FFN parameter space interpolation.
Trained from scratch, reViT-B/16 achieves DeiT III accuracy on ImageNet-1k using approximately 70% fewer stored parameters.
Distilled with an 8-expert bank using only DINOv2 output features, reViT retains linear-probe accuracy and transfers to downstream classification, segmentation, and depth prediction.
Elastic-depth training enables a single checkpoint to evaluate across flexible depths, or materialize into a static dense graph for deployment.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows vision transformers to drastically reduce stored model parameter counts and dynamically adapt execution depth without sacrificing accuracy or requiring complex per-layer distillation.

security.title: GROB: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Public-Trace Investigation of Candidate Agentic Activity

summary.tldr: GROB is a multi-agent architecture that conducts read-only collection of public Internet traces to preserve evidence for later resolution when privileged telemetry is unavailable.
key_points: Operates via controlled, read-only collection and preservation of public traces without requiring privileged telemetry.
Demonstrated trace resolution in a frozen September 2026 corpus where Census-labelled identifiers captured on September 9 were resolved via public revision records to Census requests from June 16–17.
Highlights limitations of public traces, noting that while sparse evidence supports later reconstruction, it cannot establish organizational attribution.
Identifies agent identity continuity as an unresolved challenge for autonomous language-model agents.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that sparse, unprivileged public traces can be collected proactively to successfully reconstruct past autonomous agent activity once supplementary public evidence emerges.

security.title: Characterizing Statistical Separability in TP-CRIV for Probabilistic AI Models

summary.tldr: A theoretical characterization of statistical separability in third-party challenge-response identity verification (TP-CRIV) for probabilistic AI models that quantifies verification performance based on challenge and response counts.
key_points: Formulates a statistical framework connecting challenge-wise probabilistic model behavior to system-level verification separability between matching and non-matching provers.
Derives theoretical relationships showing how the number of independent challenges and repeated responses per challenge impact the target Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC).
Provides a method to estimate the minimum required verification budget (challenge and response repetitions) needed to reach a specific target AUC.
Validated empirically on Large Language Models (LLMs) using open-ended challenges, showing close alignment between theoretical and observed AUC metrics.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a rigorous mathematical foundation to calculate the exact testing budget required to audit and verify remotely deployed probabilistic AI models without direct access to the reference model.

security.title: BRACE: Differential Privacy for Dense Associative Memory with LSR Energy

summary.tldr: The BRACE algorithm introduces a differentially private retrieval mechanism for log-sum-ReLU dense associative memory that adaptively corrects boundary-sensitive perturbations across state trajectories.
key_points: Addresses privacy challenges caused by the finite-support retrieval dynamics of log-sum-ReLU (LSR) dense associative memory (DAM).
Introduces Boundary-Responsive Adaptive Correction Evolution (BRACE) to control cumulative noise over the retrieval trajectory.
Proves minimax optimality by establishing dimension-independent terminal and full-trajectory error rates with optimal scaling for inverse temperature and retrieval horizon.
Provides central limit theorems to quantify privacy-induced variability and characterize the asymptotic distribution of private retrieval dynamics.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a theoretical baseline for dimension-independent, privacy-preserving state retrieval and uncertainty quantification in energy-based memory systems.

security.title: Speedbumps: Rejection Attacks on Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Speculative Rejection Attacks (SRAs), using adversarial suffixes to reduce draft-token acceptance rates in speculative decoding and inflate target LLM inference latency.
key_points: Attacks append adversarial suffixes to degrade draft-target distribution agreement, forcing more target-model forward passes per generated token.
Speedbump-P optimizes acceptance using the target's probability of draft proposals, while Speedbump-D optimizes based on the overlap between draft and target distributions.
Attacks can reduce inference speed below standard autoregressive decoding, transfer across different draft/target model pairings, and remain effective under sampling.
Applying regularization during suffix optimization restores output quality but reduces attack effectiveness, offering a trade-off between stealthiness and speed degradation.
summary.why_it_matters: SRAs reveal that the interaction between draft and target models is a viable attack surface, allowing malicious inputs to cause severe denial-of-service and cost inflation in speculative LLM serving systems.

security.title: PairAudit: Guiding Human Review with Graph Tokens under Distribution Shift

summary.tldr: PairAudit uses graph tokens to analyze relational prediction patterns and identify confident misclassifications under distribution shift, maximizing error correction within a fixed human review budget without retraining the detector.
key_points: Leverages graph tokens to capture relational patterns across connected nodes rather than performing feature aggregation to build a new predictor.
Identifies confident intrusion detection errors on unseen attacks where uncertainty-based and anomaly-score methods fail.
Integrates human feedback to dynamically evaluate whether identified relational anomalies justify altering review priorities.
Outperforms uncertainty-based review in average error corrections across security tasks while accounting for all review costs.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables security operations to catch novel, confident attack misclassifications under strict human auditing budgets without needing to retrain existing intrusion detection models.

security.title: Another Historic Cipher Falls to AI

summary.tldr: An 1809 historic cipher written by Napoleon's nephew has been broken using AI.
key_points: The decrypted historical ciphertext dates back to 1809.
The original document was authored by the nephew of Napoleon.
Artificial intelligence techniques were applied to successfully crack the cipher.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the efficacy of modern AI techniques in cryptanalysis for breaking historical manual ciphers.

infra.title: ICYMI: What landed for AI builders in September 2026

summary.tldr: AWS released September 2026 updates across Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and Strands, introducing OpenAI model availability, optimized agent runtime infrastructure, and new open-source developer tooling.
key_points: Amazon Bedrock added public preview support for OpenAI-powered Managed Agents with IAM permissions and CloudTrail auditability, alongside GA access to OpenAI Astra, Sol, and Luna models.
The Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime introduced lower cold-start latency, hardware-isolated execution, and pay-as-you-go serverless scaling that scales to zero when idle.
Strands released a new open-source agent harness achieving equal accuracy with 28 percent fewer tokens, accessible via Python and TypeScript.
Strands Decider 2B was launched as an open-source 2-billion parameter decision model for tool selection and routing, delivering local non-text option selection in ~115ms.
summary.why_it_matters: These updates allow enterprise developers to deploy lower-latency, token-efficient agents using top-tier models while keeping data within AWS security boundaries.

infra.title: How Postman runs Agent Mode for 40 million developers on Amazon Bedrock

summary.tldr: Postman built Agent Mode using Amazon Bedrock to provide AI-native API testing, documentation, and discovery for 40 million developers.
key_points: Agent Mode runs on Amazon Bedrock using cross-Region inference, model-dependent zero data retention, and multi-tier prompt caching to handle global traffic bursts.
Integrated Amazon Bedrock Guardrails allow enterprise administrators to automatically redact personally identifiable information (PII) before requests reach the LLM.
The system enforces human oversight by requiring explicit user approval before executing any actions that modify application state.
Postman transitioned away from highly atomic, single-field tool calls after finding that frequent round-trips to the model caused high latency in multi-step workflows.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how to scale LLM agents in production by balancing fine-grained tool orchestration, strict privacy controls, and managed infrastructure for millions of users.

infra.title: Pay-per-inference for AI agents: How BlockRun and Incarna use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments

summary.tldr: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments enables autonomous AI agents to execute sub-cent, pay-per-inference micropayments using the x402 protocol and managed cryptocurrency wallets.
key_points: Incarna integrated AgentCore payments to allow AI agents to pay BlockRun on-demand for single model inferences across 90+ models and 15+ providers.
Handles HTTP 402 ('Payment Required') responses natively by signing x402 transactions using Coinbase CDP wallets and settling on-chain with USDC on the Base network.
Enforces spending limits and governance at the infrastructure layer, preventing overspending even if the agent's prompt is manipulated.
Credentials for providers like Coinbase CDP or Stripe Privy are stored securely via AWS Secrets Manager and managed through the AgentCore SDK, CLI, or AWS SDK.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces custom billing pipelines and card networks with infrastructure-level payment signing and spending limits suited for high-frequency, sub-cent agent-to-agent transactions.
